If you want to study accounting in Australia in 2027, choosing a university is only part of the decision. You also need to compare the course itself, tuition fees, entry requirements, professional recognition, intake dates and where the qualification could realistically take you after graduation.

The short answer is that Australia remains a strong place to study accounting. International students can choose a Bachelor of Accounting, a Bachelor of Commerce with an accounting major, a Master of Professional Accounting or, in some cases, a diploma or pathway programme.

The important bit is choosing the right one.

A famous university name will not fix a course that does not fit your background, budget or professional plans. This guide focuses on the decisions a 2027 applicant actually needs to make.

What Has Changed for Accounting Students in Australia in 2027?

There is a good reason to be careful with older accounting guides.

Australia has set a National Planning Level of 295,000 new international student commencements for 2027, keeping it at the same level as 2026. Course availability therefore matters, particularly at universities with strong international demand.

There is also an accounting-specific change that still appears incorrectly in older articles.

The Accounting Professional Year Programme has closed. New students planning for 2027 should not choose an accounting degree because somebody has promised a Professional Year pathway afterwards. Instead, focus on course recognition, professional accreditation, skills and employability.

For a broader view of the application process, it can help to understand how international students typically prepare for Australian study.

Why Study Accounting in Australia?

Accounting is sometimes described as a "safe" degree. That is not quite the right way to think about it.

A better reason to study accounting is its reach.

Accountants work in public practice, banking, government, technology companies, healthcare, construction, retail, education and almost every other sector that needs financial reporting, budgeting, taxation, controls or business advice.

A well-structured accounting course can develop knowledge in:

  • financial accounting and reporting
  • management accounting
  • audit and assurance
  • taxation
  • business and corporations law
  • economics and finance
  • accounting information systems
  • business analytics
  • professional communication

Here is the thing many students realise quite late: employers do not hire an accounting graduate simply because the word "Accounting" appears on the certificate.

A graduate who can use Excel confidently, understand Xero or MYOB, interpret financial data and explain a problem clearly to a manager may have a much stronger practical profile.

There is another slightly counterintuitive point. The highest-ranked university is not automatically the best accounting choice.

Suppose one suitable degree costs AUD 47,000 a year and another costs more than AUD 60,000. Over three years, that difference becomes substantial. If both support your professional pathway, the more expensive name needs to offer something valuable enough to justify the extra cost.

That is the type of comparison worth making.

That table is only a starting point. Individual universities set their own admission requirements.

Diploma and Accounting Pathway Courses

A diploma or pathway can work well if you need an alternative entry route into university or want more practical introductory study.

Subjects may cover bookkeeping, payroll, accounting software, business records, basic taxation and financial reporting.

Do not choose a pathway simply because the first-year price looks low.

Check whether the programme appears on the official CRICOS register, whether it provides credit towards a Bachelor degree and whether the course structure supports your longer-term plan.

Students working with a tighter budget can also compare lower-cost study options in Australia before settling on one route.

Bachelor of Accounting in Australia

A Bachelor of Accounting in Australia is the most direct undergraduate option for many school leavers who already know they want an accounting-related career.

Most programmes take about three years full-time.

Typical subjects include:

  • financial accounting
  • management accounting
  • audit
  • taxation
  • business law
  • economics
  • finance
  • accounting systems

Real 2027 fees show why comparing programmes matters.

RMIT University lists its Bachelor of Accounting at approximately AUD 47,040 for a 2027 international student's annual tuition, with February and July intakes.

Macquarie University's 2027 international guide lists its Bachelor of Professional Accounting at approximately AUD 46,900 per year, also with February and July entry.

The figures are close. Other Australian universities can be considerably more expensive.

Bachelor of Commerce with an Accounting Major

A Commerce degree can make more sense if you want accounting without making your entire undergraduate programme narrowly accounting-focused.

Depending on the university, you may combine accounting with finance, economics, analytics, marketing, information systems or another business discipline.

Think about it this way.

A Bachelor of Accounting says, "I know my main field."

A Bachelor of Commerce with Accounting says, "Accounting is my main business specialisation, but I want room to build around it."

Neither is automatically better.

What matters is whether the accounting units cover the professional knowledge areas you may need later.

Master of Professional Accounting in Australia

A Master of Professional Accounting, often shortened to MPA, is particularly relevant to graduates.

Your first degree does not always need to be in accounting.

For example, someone with an engineering degree who later moved into project budgeting may not want to restart with another three-year undergraduate degree. An MPA may offer a more logical route into professional accounting study if the university accepts that applicant's previous qualification.

A typical MPA includes:

  • financial reporting
  • management accounting
  • audit
  • taxation
  • economics
  • finance
  • business law
  • accounting systems

Deakin University's 2027 Master of Professional Accounting provides a useful real-world price point. Its published estimate is approximately AUD 48,000 for a typical full-time year, with March, July and November 2027 intakes.

The actual total depends on your entry point, course length and any recognised prior learning.

Study CPA in Australia for International Students: How Does It Work?

This is one of the easiest parts of Australian accounting study to misunderstand.

CPA Australia is not simply another university accounting degree.

For many students, the route looks like this:

Eligible tertiary qualification → required accounting knowledge → CPA Program eligibility → CPA Program and professional experience requirements

CPA Australia checks whether university programmes meet its academic requirements. Before accepting an accounting offer, use the CPA Australia accredited course search to check the institution, programme and relevant study year.

Here is a simple way to think about the pathway:

Your position

What to investigate

School leaver

A recognised Bachelor accounting route

Graduate from another subject

Master of Professional Accounting

Existing accounting graduate

CPA Program eligibility

Interested in becoming a Chartered Accountant

CA ANZ academic requirements

Missing required knowledge areas

Recognised additional study or foundation requirements

CPA Australia generally expects a recognised degree comparable to Australian Bachelor level, or qualifying postgraduate study, before full progression through its professional pathway.

An accredited university degree can make that process easier, but a course not appearing in the accreditation search is not automatically useless. CPA Australia can assess qualifications individually.

The smart move is to check before enrolment rather than after graduation.

CPA Australia vs CA ANZ: What Should You Check?

CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, usually known as CA ANZ, are two major professional accounting bodies.

Students sometimes ask which one is "better". That question is too broad.

First ask whether your chosen degree covers the right academic areas.

CA ANZ identifies competence areas including:

  • Accounting Fundamentals
  • Audit and Assurance
  • Business Law
  • Economics
  • Financial Accounting and Reporting
  • Finance
  • Information and Communications Technology
  • Management Accounting
  • Taxation

You can review the current CA ANZ accredited study requirements before choosing a programme.

This matters because two universities can both advertise a "Master of Professional Accounting" while using different subject structures.

The title alone does not tell the full story.

Best Universities for Accounting in Australia

Students searching for the best universities for accounting in Australia often start with rankings.

Use rankings to create a shortlist, not to finish it.

Universities commonly considered for accounting and business study include UNSW Sydney, Monash University, University of Sydney, University of Melbourne, Macquarie University, RMIT University, Deakin University, University of Queensland, University of Western Australia and University of Technology Sydney.

Accounting Degree Cost in Australia

The accounting degree cost in Australia varies widely enough that using one national figure can be misleading.

A practical 2027 planning range is:

Course

Indicative annual tuition

Diploma or pathway

AUD 8,000 to AUD 25,000

Bachelor of Accounting

AUD 25,000 to AUD 55,000+

Bachelor of Commerce with Accounting

AUD 30,000 to AUD 60,000+

Master of Professional Accounting

AUD 30,000 to AUD 62,000+

Higher-fee business programmes

Can exceed AUD 60,000

For comparison, an international student paying about AUD 46,900 to AUD 48,000 per year faces roughly AUD 140,000 to AUD 144,000 in tuition over a three-year Bachelor programme if fees stayed unchanged.

They usually do not stay unchanged.

Universities commonly review international tuition each year, so leave room for annual increases in your budget.

What Else Does an International Student Need to Pay?

Tuition is only one line.

You should also budget for:

  • Overseas Student Health Cover
  • flights
  • accommodation bond and advance rent
  • food
  • transport
  • books or software
  • laptop and study equipment
  • emergency expenses

For a city-level estimate, the Study Australia cost-of-living calculator is more useful than guessing from somebody else's monthly budget.

OSHC is another unavoidable planning item for most students. Understanding how health cover fits into your Australian study budget can prevent a surprise after you receive an offer.

Scholarships for Accounting Students in Australia

Scholarships can reduce the cost, but treat them as an advantage rather than the foundation of your financial plan.

Universities offer different types of support:

  • academic merit awards
  • international student grants
  • country-specific grants
  • faculty scholarships
  • tuition discounts
  • leadership scholarships

Some current 2027 examples are quite concrete.

Monash University has published international study grants of AUD 5,000, AUD 10,000 or AUD 15,000 for eligible applicants from selected countries, including Bangladesh, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Vietnam.

Other awards use percentage tuition reductions rather than a fixed amount.

That leads to a sensible budgeting rule: shortlist courses you can realistically finance without winning a scholarship, then calculate how an award would improve the position.

Accounting Requirements in Australia for International Students

Accounting requirements in Australia depend on the course level and university.

Bachelor Entry Requirements

A Bachelor applicant will generally need:

  • a recognised secondary qualification comparable to Australian Year 12
  • the required academic result
  • English-language evidence
  • academic transcripts and certificates
  • passport or identity documents
  • any subject prerequisites required by the university

Some accounting or Commerce courses may require mathematics. Others may not.

Check the exact programme.

Master of Professional Accounting Entry Requirements

A Master's applicant will usually need:

  • a recognised Bachelor degree
  • the university's minimum academic result
  • English-language evidence
  • academic transcripts
  • passport
  • any additional documents requested for the application

Many Master of Professional Accounting programmes accept students who did not major in accounting before.

That is one reason the MPA has become a popular accounting conversion route for international graduates.

English Language Requirements

IELTS Academic requirements around 6.0 to 6.5 overall are common across Australian business programmes, although minimum component scores vary.

Universities may also accept alternatives such as PTE Academic or TOEFL iBT.

If your academic history includes a long break, it is also worth understanding how to present a study gap for Australia before submitting an application.

2027 Intakes for Accounting Courses in Australia

February or March and July remain the main intake periods for accounting courses, but not every university follows the same calendar.

For example:

University and course

February, July

That third intake can matter.

A student who misses a mid-year application at one university may still have a later postgraduate option elsewhere. On the other hand, assuming every programme has three intakes can create a costly delay.

Always check the course page, not just the university's general academic calendar.

Jobs and Skills Australia reports median full-time earnings of about AUD 2,003 per week before tax for Accountants.

You can check the official labour-market profile for Accountants for the underlying occupation data.

One caution matters here.

That figure is an occupation-wide median. It is not a guaranteed graduate starting salary.

Skills make a difference too. Learn the accounting theory, but do not stop there. Excel, accounting software, Power BI, communication and workplace experience can separate two graduates who technically hold similar degrees.

Post-Study Work and PR Planning

Many international students ask whether accounting is a PR course in Australia.

There is no accounting degree that guarantees permanent residency.

Permanent residency can depend on:

  • occupation eligibility
  • skills assessment
  • English score
  • age
  • points
  • employment history
  • state or territory nomination
  • future policy changes

Accounting can form part of skilled migration planning, but the order matters.

Choose a qualification that works academically and professionally first. Then assess migration options under the rules that apply when you become eligible.

For deeper planning, compare possible PR routes after Australian study with course areas students often consider for skilled migration.

How to Choose the Right Accounting Course

Before paying a tuition deposit, ask these questions:

Question

What a good answer looks like

Is the course CRICOS-registered?

The exact programme has a valid registration

Does it fit my previous study?

The academic progression makes sense

Does it support CPA or CA requirements?

Accreditation or required subject coverage is clear

Can I afford the full programme?

Tuition and living costs remain manageable

Is my 2027 intake available?

The exact course accepts students in your intended period

Does the city fit my budget?

Housing and transport remain realistic

Does the course build practical skills?

Applied projects, technology or work experience are included

Location deserves more attention than it usually gets.

A university that saves you AUD 3,000 in annual tuition may not actually be cheaper if accommodation costs thousands more each year.

Compare Australian cities from a student-budget perspective alongside course fees.

Then shortlist three to five realistic options rather than applying to every university you recognise.

If the differences are still difficult to judge, you can talk through your shortlist with an adviser before submitting applications.

Frequently Asked Questions About Studying Accounting in Australia

Is accounting good to study in Australia?

Yes. Accounting can be a strong choice for international students interested in financial reporting, audit, taxation, management accounting, finance operations and advisory work. Choose a programme with suitable subjects, professional recognition and practical career support.

How much does it cost to study accounting in Australia?

Which university is best for accounting in Australia?

There is no single best university for every accounting student. Universities such as UNSW, Monash, Macquarie, RMIT, Deakin, Melbourne, Sydney, UQ, UWA and UTS are commonly considered. Compare the exact programme, accreditation, fees, intake and location rather than rankings alone.

Can international students study CPA in Australia?

International students can work towards CPA Australia membership, but CPA Australia is not simply a university accounting degree. Students generally need an eligible tertiary qualification and must meet CPA Australia's academic requirements before progressing through the professional pathway.

How long does an accounting degree take in Australia?

A Bachelor of Accounting normally takes around three years full-time. A Master of Professional Accounting commonly takes about 1.5 to 2 years, although prior study and recognised credit can change the duration.

What subjects are needed to study accounting in Australia?

University accounting programmes commonly include financial accounting, management accounting, taxation, auditing, business law, economics, finance and accounting information systems. Admission prerequisites differ by university.

What are the entry requirements for accounting in Australia?

Bachelor applicants usually need a recognised Year 12 equivalent qualification and English-language evidence. Master's applicants generally need a recognised Bachelor degree plus the required academic and English results.

Can I study accounting in Australia without IELTS?

What are the main 2027 accounting intakes in Australia?

February or March and July are the most common. Some universities offer additional intakes. Deakin's Master of Professional Accounting, for example, lists March, July and November entry for 2027.

Is accounting good for PR in Australia?

Accounting can connect with skilled migration pathways, but studying accounting does not guarantee Australian permanent residency. Future eligibility depends on the occupation, skills assessment, English, points, age, work history, nomination and migration policy at the time.

Final Advice

If you plan to study accounting in Australia in 2027, start with the programme rather than the university logo.

Check the subjects. Check CRICOS registration. Check CPA Australia or CA ANZ recognition if professional accounting matters to you.

Then look at the numbers.

Tuition, scholarship possibilities, course duration, living expenses and the city can completely change which offer represents better value.

A prestigious university with the wrong course structure or an unrealistic total cost is not automatically the best decision.

Choose an accounting programme that fits your background, makes financial sense and leaves you with useful professional options after graduation. That is a much stronger starting point than choosing a course because somebody simply called it "the best".
